[readme.txt]
here are the source data files used for the model-data comparison presented in the article. the experimental data are present in the presence-absence.csv file, while the computed model outputs are split into a node and edges files.

== description of data files ==

1. presence-absence.csv - experimental data, copied from the data folder

-----------------------------

2. nodes.csv - contains the list of all nodes (sets of species) in the computed transition network (see gaucherel & pommereau 2019).

- "node" corresponds to the node identifier
- "succ" to its successors allowed by rules
- "pred" to its possible predecessors
- "on" to the species which are present in the node
- "off" to the species which are present in the node
- "dead" is "vrai" (true) when the state is a deadlock, and "faux" (false) otherwise
- "transient" is irrelevant here
- "component" corresponds to the identifier of the graph component (set of nodes which share the same possible outcome)
- "kind" corresponds to the kind of state (basin has several possible outcomes, plotted as diamonds in the paper ; dead+basin only one outcome, plotted as squares)
- "size" corresponds to the number of nodes in the component.

nb: a variable "i" can be seen in the "on" and "off" columns, it corresponds to nodes used as starting points for computing the model. all nodes there "i" is on are starting points and ignored in the computations.

-----------------------------

3. edges.csv - contains the list of all edges of the computed transition network

- "src" is the identifier of the source node
- "dst" is the identifier of the destination node
- "rules" is the list of rules allowing to go from the source node to the destination node: 
r1: a+ >> p-
r2: a+ >> a-
r3: a+, p- >> b-
r4: a+, p- >> t-
r5: b+ >> t-
r6: e+ >> e-
r7: e+ >> t-
r8: c+ >> t-
r9: p+ >> t-
r10: c+ >> c-
r11-r17 correspond to the initialization of nodes from variable i and disappearance of variable i ; it's a computation trick to compute the whole graph of possible states and transitions rather than starting from a given node. they are ignored in the computations.

[readme.txt]
1) data_summary correspond to the supplementary s1 table, in latex and csv format.

2) measured_traj.csv is an update of the 'edges.csv' file present in the 'data/' folder, with two new colums:
- "n" corresponds to the number of times the transition was observed in the dataset,
- "measured" is 1 if the transition was observed and 0 if it wasn't.

title: Data from: The determinants of tropical forest deciduousness: disentangling the effects of rainfall and geology in central Africa
codebook:
[README_for_Data_OuedraogoEtAl2016_JEcol.txt]
Data from Oudraogo D.-Y., Fayolle A., Gourlet-Fleury S., Mortier F., Freycon V., Fauvet N., Rabaud S., Cornu G., Bndet F., Gillet J.-F., Oslisly R., Doucet J.-L., Lejeune P., Favier C. (2016). The determinants of tropical forest deciduousness: disentangling the effects of rainfall and geology in central Africa.

Journal of Ecology

For more information on data contact dakis.ouedraogo@gmail.com or fabrice.benedet@cirad.fr or sylvie.gourlet-fleury@cirad.fr


We provide a zip file containing three txt files used in the analyses presented in the article (columns delimited with semicolons ";", encoding "UTF-8", decimal point represented with a dot ".").

The species_trait.txt file contains the species x traits data (767 species or morphospecies, 2 traits). A description of the two species traits, i.e. species regeneration guild sensus Hawthorne (1995, "regen_guild") and species leaf habit ("leaf_habit"), is given below.

The plot_gen_trait.txt file contains the plot x genera x traits data (62 624 plots, "plot", and 247 genera, "anonym_gen"). To respect the industrial secret imposed by the logging companies on the vegetation data we provide anonymous genera names with their corresponding traits (see description below). 

The plot.txt file contains plot location (coordinates in decimal degree, "plot_x" and "plot_y"), area ("surf", in ha), corresponding cell on the 8x8km grid ("cell"), coordinates of the corresponding cell ("cell_x" and "cell_y"), geological substrate ("geol"), HWSD soil map unit ("hwsd_smu", Harmonized World Soil Database, FAO et al. 2008), most common soil type ("dominant_soil", see the key to the FAO Soil Units (1974) for a legend, http://www.fao.org/soils-portal/soil-survey/soil-classification/fao-legend/key-to-the-fao-soil-units/en/), proportion of the most common soil type in the soil map unit ("soil_prop", %), monthly rainfall (from "rain1" to "rain12", in mm, modified from WorldClim data, Hijmans et al. 2005), monthly potential evapotranspiration (from "etp1" to "etp12", in mm, CGIAR-CSI Global Aridity and Global-PET database, Zomer et al. 2007, 2008), annual rainfall ("rain_total", in mm), annual potential evapotranspiration ("etp_total", in mm), and maximum climatological water deficit ("MCWD", in mm, computed from monthly rainfall and potential evapotranspiration).

------------------------------------------------------------------------
Variable description:

Code        Description

"regen_guild"
pP          Short-lived pioneer (considering that pioneers require gap for establishment)
gP          Long-lived pioneer
NPLD        Non-pioneer light-demanding (can establish in shade but need a gap to grow to their full height)
SB          Shade-bearer (can be found in shade both as young and older plants)
?           Undetermined

"leaf_habit"
deci        Deciduous (totally leafless for some period of the year)
ever        Evergreen (replacement of leaves throughout the year)
leafexch    Leaf-exchang

title: Rapid Documentation Avifaunal Diversity of Buxa Tiger Reserve, Alipurduar, West Bengal, India
codebook:
[buxa zenodo.txt]
﻿Rapid Documentation Avifaunal Diversity of Buxa Tiger Reserve, Alipurduar, West Bengal, India
The dataset “Rapid Documentation Avifaunal Diversity of Buxa Tiger Reserve, Alipurduar, West Bengal, India” is published by Nature Mates Nature Club
Buxa Tiger Reserve is a tiger reserve and national park lies in the Alipurduar district of northern West Bengal, India, covering an area of 760 km2.
Buxa Tiger Reserve was created in 1983 as the 15th tiger reserve in India. In 1986, Buxa Wildlife Sanctuary constituted over 314.52 km2 of the reserve forests. In 1991, 54.47 km2 was added to Buxa Wildlife Sanctuary. A year later, in 1992, the Government of West Bengal declared its intentions to constitute a national park over 117.10 km2 of the Buxa Wildlife Sanctuary. State government finally declared the national park with notification No.3403-For/11B-6/95 dt. 05.12.1997.
Buxa Tiger Reserve(BTR) lies in Alipurduar district of West Bengal. Its northern boundary runs along the international border with Bhutan
It is the easternmost extension of extreme bio-diverse North-East India and represents highly endemic Indo-Malayan region. The fragile "Terai Eco-System" constitutes a part of this reserve. The Phibsoo Wildlife Sanctuary of Bhutan is contiguous to the north of BTR. Manas National Park lies on east of BTR. BTR, thus, serves as an international corridor for Asian elephant migration between India and Bhutan. To the south-west, the Chilapata Forests form an elephant corridor to the Jaldapara Wildlife Sanctuary.
The forest type of the reserve includes : Northern dry deciduous, Eastern Bhabar and Terai sal, East Himalayan moist mixed deciduous forest, Sub-Himalayan secondary wet mixed forest, Eastern sub-montane semi-evergreen forest, Northern tropical evergreen forest, East Himalayan subtropical wet hill forest, Moist sal savannah, Low alluvium, Savannah woodland.(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buxa_Tiger_Reserve, http://www.wildbengal.com/buxa.php).The main species constitutes trees like Sal, Champ, Gamar, Simul, Chikrasi. 
The climate of the reserve is mostly humid subtropical with hot summers and cool winters. The monsoon season begins in June and lasts until September, bringing heavy rainfall to the region. (https://www.studyiq.com/articles/buxa-tiger-reserve/)
So far 352 species of trees, 133 species of shrubs, 189 species of herbs, 108 species of climbers, 144 species of orchids, 46 species of grasses,16 species of sedges, 6 species of canes and 4 species of bamboos have been reported. Buxa has a good faunal diversity. As many as 68 species of mammals, 41 species of reptiles, more than 246 species of birds, 4 species of Amphibians along with 103 species of fishes and around 500 species of insects have been recorded.(https://ntca.gov.in/assets/uploads/briefnote/buxa.pdf)
This dataset enlists all the birds identified during a biodiversity survey conducted in the year 2016
Species or genus-level identifications have been made for every species. Ther

﻿rapid documentation avifaunal diversity of buxa tiger reserve, alipurduar, west bengal, india
the dataset “rapid documentation avifaunal diversity of buxa tiger reserve, alipurduar, west bengal, india” is published by nature mates nature club
buxa tiger reserve is a tiger reserve and national park lies in the alipurduar district of northern west bengal, india, covering an area of 760 km2.
buxa tiger reserve was created in 1983 as the 15th tiger reserve in india. in 1986, buxa wildlife sanctuary constituted over 314.52 km2 of the reserve forests. in 1991, 54.47 km2 was added to buxa wildlife sanctuary. a year later, in 1992, the government of west bengal declared its intentions to constitute a national park over 117.10 km2 of the buxa wildlife sanctuary. state government finally declared the national park with notification no.3403-for/11b-6/95 dt. 05.12.1997.
buxa tiger reserve(btr) lies in alipurduar district of west bengal. its northern boundary runs along the international border with bhutan
it is the easternmost extension of extreme bio-diverse north-east india and represents highly endemic indo-malayan region. the fragile "terai eco-system" constitutes a part of this reserve. the phibsoo wildlife sanctuary of bhutan is contiguous to the north of btr. manas national park lies on east of btr. btr, thus, serves as an international corridor for asian elephant migration between india and bhutan. to the south-west, the chilapata forests form an elephant corridor to the jaldapara wildlife sanctuary.
the forest type of the reserve includes : northern dry deciduous, eastern bhabar and terai sal, east himalayan moist mixed deciduous forest, sub-himalayan secondary wet mixed forest, eastern sub-montane semi-evergreen forest, northern tropical evergreen forest, east himalayan subtropical wet hill forest, moist sal savannah, low alluvium, savannah woodland.(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/buxa_tiger_reserve, http://www.wildbengal.com/buxa.php).the main species constitutes trees like sal, champ, gamar, simul, chikrasi. 
the climate of the reserve is mostly humid subtropical with hot summers and cool winters. the monsoon season begins in june and lasts until september, bringing heavy rainfall to the region. (https://www.studyiq.com/articles/buxa-tiger-reserve/)
so far 352 species of trees, 133 species of shrubs, 189 species of herbs, 108 species of climbers, 144 species of orchids, 46 species of grasses,16 species of sedges, 6 species of canes and 4 species of bamboos have been reported. buxa has a good faunal diversity. as many as 68 species of mammals, 41 species of reptiles, more than 246 species of birds, 4 species of amphibians along with 103 species of fishes and around 500 species of insects have been recorded.(https://ntca.gov.in/assets/uploads/briefnote/buxa.pdf)
this dataset enlists all the birds identified during a biodiversity survey conducted in the year 2016
species or genus-level identifications have been made for every species. ther

title: Data from: Successional status, seed dispersal mode and overstorey species influence tree regeneration in tropical rain-forest fragments in Western Ghats, India
codebook:
[osuri_et_al_metadata.txt]
This dataset corresponds to the following publication:
Osuri, A. M., Chakravarthy, D., Mudappa, D., Raman, T. R. S., Ayyappan, N., Muthuramkumar, S., and Parthasarathy, N. 2017. Successional status, seed dispersal mode and overstorey species influence tree regeneration in tropical rain-forest fragments in Western Ghats, India. Journal of Tropical Ecology 33: 270-284. DOI: 10.1017/S0266467417000219

This is version 2 of the dataset with data provided in CSV format. Version 1 (http://datadryad.org/resource/doi:10.5061/dryad.vd0nn) contains the same data in .xlsx format.

The download includes a compressed folder that contains three CSV files whose contents are described below:
1) osuri_et_al_trees_regen_data.csv
2) osuri_et_al_trees_adult_data.csv
3) osuri_et_al_trees_traits_data.csv

-----File 1: "osuri_et_al_trees_regen_data.csv"-----
Description: The file contains records of all seedlings and saplings (1-5 cm diameter at breast height of 1.3 m, dbh) and larger trees (>5 cm dbh) recorded within 5m x 5m regeneration plots that were nested within 20m x 20m adult tree plots in two continuous forests and two forest fragments. Data were filtered during analysis to retain only seedling and saplings, defined as individuals with effective diameter <=5 cm.

title: Functional diversity of the avian assemblages better than taxonomic diversity in capturing the effect of protection
codebook:
[README.txt]
﻿-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
				         README
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This folder consists of four input files (.RDS) and one R script file (.R). These files are part of the publication "Functional diversity of the avian assemblages better than taxonomic diversity in capturing the effect of protection".
The figures generated in the R platform were exported in svg format and annotated in Inkscape software.

The description of four input files are as follows:

1.kba_data.rds: This file provides the raw dataset obtained as part of the Kerala Bird Atlas. This file contains following 9 columns-
"Common.Name" - Standard English names of the species detected during the Kerala Bird Atlas.
"Date" - Date of survey.
"Time" - Time of survey.
"n.observers" - Number of observers in the survey team.
"County" - District name.
"Sub.cell" - Unique code assigned to every surveyed sub-cell.
"Season" - Survey season; wet or dry.
"Cell.ID" - Unique code assigned to every surveyed cell.
"List.ID" - Unique checklist ID.
The geographic locations and List IDs of Great Hornbill (Buceros bicornis) records have not been provided since it is a sensitive species (https://ebird.org/india/news/ebird-sensitive-species). 

2.kba_names.rds: This file provides the list of species which were included in the analysis and taxa ('Spuhs','Slashes', Nocturnal and Pelagic species) which were eliminated from the raw dataset.
This file has following 4 columns-
"Common.Name"  - Standard English names of the species detected during the Kerala Bird Atlas.
"Scientific.Name" - Standard Binomial names of the species detected during the Kerala Bird Atlas.
"Action" - Suggests whether the species is to be reassigned a new name or is to be removed. e.g., 'Rock Pigeon' renamed to 'Rock Pigeon (Feral)'.    
"Assigned.Name.for.Atlas" - Provides the Standard English names or assigned names for all the species included in the analysis.

3.kba_species.details.rds: This file provides the details of 361 species detected during the Kerala Bird Atlas. Its 32 columns provides following information-
"Common.Name","Scientific.Name","Resident.status","IUCN.Redlist.Status","Distribution.Status","SoIB.status",
"Taxonomic order","Taxonomic Family","Endemicity","ForagingStrata","TrophicNiche","Diet.Inv","Diet.Vend",
"Diet.Vect","Diet.Vfish","Diet.Vunk","Diet.Scav","Diet.Fruit","Diet.Nect","Diet.Seed","Diet.PlantO",
"BodyMass.Value","Adult.survival","Maximum.longevity","Mean.clutch.size",
"Beak.Length","Beak.Width","Beak.Depth","Tarsus","Wing","HWI" (Hand-wing-index),"Tail"  


#################################################################
######Details of traits used in the analyses are as follows######
#################################################################

>>Morphometric data (Source-Stewart et al. 2021): Beak l

title: Data on rainforest birds from line transect surveys in the Kalakad - Mundathurai Tiger Reserve, Tamil Nadu, India
codebook:
[README.TXT]
This dataset contains data on rainforest bird communities collected along line transects in Kalakad - Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve, Tamil Nadu, India, as part of doctoral research leading up to the following thesis:
Raman, T. R. S. 2001. Community ecology and conservation of mid-elevation tropical rainforest bird communities in the southern Western Ghats, India. PhD thesis, Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore.

Part of the data (from transects T2 and T3, in particular) was used in the following publication:
Raman, T. R. S. 2003. Assessment of census techniques for inter-specific comparisons of tropical rainforest bird densities. Ibis 145: 9-21. http://doi.org/10.1046/j.1474-919X.2003.00105.x

The Raman (2003) publication also uses bird point count data (from T2 and T3) available in a related dataset:  
Raman, T. R. S.,  Mudappa, D., Jeganathan, P., Joshi, N. V., Sukumar, R. 2022. Data on bird communities and vegetation in relation to altitude and habitat alteration in the Kalakad - Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve, Tamil Nadu, India. Dryad, Dataset, https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.41ns1rngj

GEOGRAPHICAL AREA: Kalakad-Mundathurai Tiger Reserve (KMTR), 895 km² sanctuary located between 8°25′ to 8°53′ N and 77°10′ to 77°35′ E in Tamil Nadu state in the Western Ghats mountain range of India.

TAXONOMIC SCOPE: Birds, mammals

ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: I am grateful to P. Pavithra for help with data entry and compilation.

Besides this file (README.TXT), this dataset contains the following 3 comma-delimited text files with data in columns as explained below.

01_transectlocations.csv
This file contains details of transect in mature rainforests and plantations and plantation-forest edges
Transect: Unique ID number or name of a 600 m long line transect
LatitudeN: Approximate latitude in decimal degrees North of the midpoint of the transect
LongitudeE: Approximate longitude in decimal degrees East of the midpoint of the transect
LocationDetails: Description of location

02_transectbirds.csv
This file contains the data on birds from 5 minute variable radius point count surveys
Transect: Unique ID number or name of a 600 m long line transect
Date: Date of survey of the specified line transect
StartTime: Start time of the transect (transects were supposed to be of 60 min duration in morning hours)
EndTime: End time of the transect (transects were supposed to be of 60 min duration in morning hours)
Startweather: Weather at the start of the transect
Endweather: Weather at the end of the transect
Time: Specific time of observation
Species_old: Old common name of the bird species
Species: English common name (India) of the bird species as used in the Ebird India portal in 2022 
BirdMamm: Category indicating Bird or Mammal
Flock: Category indicating whether the observation of that species was of a detection (1 or more birds detected as indicated in the next column) or a flock of birds (a flock of more than 1 individual was present but could not be counted and is just recorded a

TNo: Unique ID number or name of a 600 m long line transect
Date: Date of survey of the specified point
StTime: Start time of the point count
Pt: ID of the surveyed point along the 600 m long transect. Most transects started at A1 and had points marked every 25 m in 100 m chunks: A1...A4, B1...B4, ... upto F1...F4, after which it ended with X at the 600 m point. Alphabet codes may vary on longer trails and in some trails the numbers 1-25 were used to mark the points.

Remark: Notes and remarks (includes some codes: *: in mixed species flock; E: detected within the point sampling area while entering;  X: detected within point sampling area while leaving;  diff/DIFF/DF: different detection from conspecific; detected on the same point; GP: flock; CC: counter-calling individuals) 

3) 03_Birdnames.csv: This file contains bird species codes and matching commo

title: Kerala Bird Atlas 2015-2020: features, outcomes and implications of a citizen-science project
codebook:
[ReadME.txt]
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
				KERALA BIRD ATLAS DATASET - README
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This folder consists of three input files (.RDS), one shape file (.shp) and one R script file (.R) for the analyses performed using the Kerala Bird Atlas: 2015-2020 dataset. 
These files are part of the publication "Kerala Bird Atlas 2015-2020: features, outcomes and implications of a citizen-science Project". There are no usage restrictions for this dataset except that all usages should provide an attribution as below

Kerala Bird Atlas Dataset (2021) Website Link. Accessed on DD Month Year

The outputs of this script are in the forms of shapefiles (.shp) and the attribute table contains the measured metrics.

This shapefile can be opened in QGIS/ArcGIS and the particular metric can be plotted.
In the script, only wet season data has been analyzed and the shapefiles have been generated. 
Dry season data can be analyzed by changing the word 'wet' to 'Dry' in the script and re-running the script.

The figures generated in the R platform were exported in svg format and annotated in Inkscape software.

The Cell IDs, Sub-cell IDs and List IDs of Great Hornbill (Buceros bicornis) records have not been provided since it is a sensitive species (https://ebird.org/india/news/ebird-sensitive-species). District names have been retained. Users interested in analyzing KBA records of Great Hornbill from any region (across Kerala or any district) may obtain the occurrence data from eBird by following due procedure for sensitive species (https://ebird.org/data/download/ebd), and get in touch with us for further assistance.

Contact:
Dr. P.O. Nameer, 
Professor (Wildlife), 
Kerala Agricultural University, Thrissur
nameer.po@kau.in

title: The thermal niche and phylogenetic assembly of evergreen tree metacommunities in a mid-to-upper tropical montane zone
codebook:
[README.txt]
This dataset contains three data files and supplementary image of the phylogenetic tree used
in analysis.

The first data file called 'Dasetal2022_Nilgiris_spabundancebysite.csv' contains species
abundance data for each of the study plots.

The second data file called 'Dasetal2022_Nilgiris_focalsplist.csv' contains the data on study 
species which was used as input to create the phylogenetic tree in the R software
package 'v.phylomaker'. Empty cells are marked as 'NA'.

The third data file called 'Dasetal2022_Nilgiri_shola_env.csv' contains the data for
each of the microclimatic and macroclimatic predictors used in the analysis.
The columns in this file are as follows:

Column		Description
Plot.no	- Number of the 20x20m vegetation plot used to sample tree and shrub species > 1cm dbh
mean.diur.tmp.rng - Mean Diurnal Range (Mean of monthly (max temp - min temp)); (bio2 in BIOCLIM v.2 dataset, Fick and Hijmans 2017)
tmp.seas - Temperature Seasonality (standard deviation *100); (bio4 in BIOCLIM v2 dataset, Fick and Hijmans 2017)
max.tmp.warm - Max Temperature of Warmest Month; (bio5 in BIOCLIM v2 dataset, Fick and Hijmans 2017)
min.tmp.cold - Min Temperature of Coldest Month; (bio6 in BIOCLIM v2 dataset, Fick and Hijmans 2017)
prec.seas - Precipitation Seasonality (Coefficient of Variation); (bio15 in BIOCLIM v2 dataset, Fick and Hijmans 2017)
elevation - Elevation in mASL
elev.zone - zone 1: 1700-1999m; zone 2: 2000 - 2199m; zone 3: 2200 - 2500m
ln.area - ln of shola forest patch area
d.edge - distance from nearest shola forest edge in meters
